title: services: loyalty, chiefs and conquering villages
criteria:
Implement loyalty and village conquest (BUILD.md T21). IMPORTANT editing rule: do NOT rewrite realm/services/military.py or realm/services/villages.py as whole files; use small targeted Edit operations only (these files contain proofread Thai strings that must stay byte-identical). New logic goes into the NEW file realm/services/conquest.py.

== realm/services/conquest.py (new) ==
`apply_loyalty(s, *, target: Village, attacker_player: Player, damage: int, now, cfg) -> dict` returns {'before': float, 'after': float, 'conquered': bool}: before = target.loyalty; damage <= 0 or target.is_capital -> unchanged, conquered False; otherwise target.loyalty = max(0.0, before - damage); when the new loyalty is <= 0 the village is conquered via `conquer_village` and 'conquered' is True. `conquer_village(s, target: Village, new_owner: Player, now, cfg) -> None`: 1) old_owner = the Player of target.player_id; call villages.settle_player_culture for BOTH players first (so culture accrues with the old ownership); 2) delete every Troop row with home_village_id == target.id (the old owner's units die, wherever they are located); 3) delete every Movement row with from_village_id == target.id and status 'moving' and cancel its pending MOVEMENT_ARRIVE event with events.cancel_pending(s, target.world_id, EventType.MOVEMENT_ARRIVE, {'movement_id': id}); 4) delete every TrainingQueue row of the village and cancel its TRAIN_TICK events (payload {'training_id': id}); 5) target.player_id = new_owner.id; target.is_capital = False; target.loyalty = cfg.combat.conquest_loyalty; 6) villages.after_change(s, target, now, cfg); notify both players (kind 'village', village id); 7) reports (kind 'info'): to the old owner titled f'ถูกยึดหมู่บ้าน {target.name}' and to the new owner titled f'ยึดหมู่บ้าน {target.name} สำเร็จ', data {'village': {'id','name','x','y'}}.

== realm/services/villages.py (small Edit) ==
In `settle_village`, when the village loyalty is below 100 (query the palace level only in that case: villages.levels(...).get('palace', 0)): before res_updated_at is advanced, loyalty = min(100.0, loyalty + palace_level * cfg.combat.loyalty_regen_per_palace_level * world.speed * elapsed_hours) with elapsed_hours = (now - res_updated_at).total_seconds()/3600. No palace -> no regeneration. Nothing else changes.

== realm/services/military.py (small Edit inside `_resolve_battle_arrival`) ==
After the loot is computed and BEFORE the return movement is created: if result.loyalty_damage > 0 call info = conquest.apply_loyalty(s, target=target, attacker_player=attacker_player, damage=result.loyalty_damage, now=now, cfg=cfg); when info['conquered'] remove the key 'chief' from `survivors` (all chiefs are consumed); store info in the report data under the existing key 'loyalty' (it is currently None: use None when there was no damage, else the info dict). Everything else in that function stays. Import conquest inside the function or at module top (conquest must not import military at module import time: if conquest needs nothing from military there is no cycle).

== Tests == tests/services/test_conquest.py (DB fixtures `s`, `cfg`, `t0`; world = worlds.create_world(s, seed=1, speed=1, player_name='ผู้เล่น', tribe='stonehold', bot_count=2, cfg=cfg, real_now=t0); A = the human's village at (0,0), B = bot 1's village moved to (7,0) with is_capital set False, C = bot 2's village; Movement rows are inserted directly: Movement(world_id, player_id=human id, from_village_id=A.id, to_x=7, to_y=0, to_village_id=B.id, mission='attack', units={'swordsman': 1000, 'chief': 2}, loot={}, departed_at, arrive_at, status='moving') and military.resolve_arrival(s, movement.id, arrive_at, cfg) is called; B stock/res_updated_at = arrival time so settling adds nothing). Hand-computed: attack power 1000*40 + 2*40 = 40080 vs defense 10 (no defenders, no wall), attacker wins with zero losses (int(1002*(10/40080)**1.5+0.5) == 0), loyalty damage = the sum of two rng.randint(20, 30) draws of random.Random(f'{world.seed}:{movement.id}') (compute the expected value in the test with that same stdlib Random). Cases: (1) B.loyalty 100 -> after = 100 - damage (between 60 and 20), owner unchanged, a 'return' Movement from A containing {'swordsman': 1000, 'chief': 2}, the battle report data['loyalty'] == {'before': 100.0, 'after': 100.0 - damage, 'conquered': False}; (2) B.loyalty 25 (<= 2*20 so always conquered): B.player_id == human player id, B.is_capital False, B.loyalty == 25.0 (cfg.combat.conquest_loyalty), the return Movement units == {'swordsman': 1000} (no chief), battle report loyalty conquered True, plus 'info' reports titled 'ถูกยึดหมู่บ้าน <B name>' for the old owner and 'ยึดหมู่บ้าน <B name> สำเร็จ' for the human; side effects: Troop(home=B, location=C, 'spearman', 7) deleted, a TrainingQueue row of B and its pending TRAIN_TICK event deleted, a moving Movement from B (mission 'raid') deleted together with its pending MOVEMENT_ARRIVE event; culture of both players was settled at the arrival time (cp_updated_at == arrival time for both); (3) capital: B.is_capital True and loyalty 25 -> loyalty stays 25.0, owner unchanged, report conquered False; (4) a failed attack (attacker too weak: units {'swordsman': 1, 'chief': 1} vs 1000 defending spearmen at B) applies no loyalty damage and report loyalty is None; (5) regeneration: B.loyalty 50, palace level 5 in B (insert Building at a center slot), villages.settle_village at +2 h -> 60.0 (5 * 1.0 * speed 1 * 2 h); loyalty 98 with the same palace after +2 h -> 100.0 (capped); no palace -> unchanged; a speed 10 world (create a second world in its own test): palace 5, loyalty 20, +1 h -> 70.0 (5*1.0*10*1).
notes:
- Thai strings: use ONLY f'ถูกยึดหมู่บ้าน {name}' and f'ยึดหมู่บ้าน {name} สำเร็จ' (copy letter by letter, proofread). No other new Thai. Do not touch any other Thai string in existing files.
- models: Troop(home_village_id, location_village_id, unit, count), Movement, TrainingQueue(village_id, ...), Village(loyalty, is_capital, player_id), Player. Real columns only in tests.
- events.cancel_pending(s, world_id, EventType.X, match_dict) -> int; reports.create_report(s, player_id, kind, title, data, now); notify.notify(s, world_id, player_ids, kind, village_id).
- The reports of the battle itself are created by existing code; keep the report creation order (the loyalty dict must be known before the report data is assembled).
- Never commit; never call datetime.now().
